RIPv2 has a faster convergence time and is more stable than OSPF.
RIPv2 is the most stable and consistent protocol in small and condensed network.
RIPv2 is the most suitable routing protocol for small networks, EIGRP is the most suitable for medium and large networks, and OSPF is most suitable for large networks.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

EIGRP has better performance than OSPF in small and condensed network, and OSPF has better performance than EIGRP in medium sized and relatively large networks, and RIPv2 has the best performance for very small networks.
EIGRP is the most stable routing protocol in both small and large networks.
EIGRP is the most stable and consistent routing protocol among the three.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have analyzed and compared a set of routing protocols, including RIPv2, OSPF, and EIGRP.
we have conducted extensive experiments to analyze and compare the performances of three different routing protocols, RIPv2, OSPF, and EIGRP by using sophisticated simulation tool called OPNET.
we used OPNET to simulate the behavior of RIPv2, OSPF and EGRP in different networks and different topologies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of routing protocols is not just a function of the protocol itself, but also of the underlying network architecture.
the performance of a routing protocol depends on the characteristics of the network.
, in general, the more complex a routing protocol is, the less stable it is.
